qs.q: SCALE: The scale of a map or chart is the ratio of a given distance on the map or chart to the actual distance it represents on the Earth. The scale of a chart at any point may be expressed in several ways. The four examples of scale descriptions given below refer to the same chart, and all four are correct:
o: 1 inch to 1 statute mile (one statute mile being 63,360 inches).

qs.q: Ratio of Map Distance to Earth Distance is called scale. On a map, scale is given by following. Representative fraction (rf) Statement in words • Graduated scale. REPRESENTATIVE FRACTION:
o: Scale on map is given in a fraction with numerator always as 1.

qs.q: The smaller the denominator of the representative fraction, the larger the scale of the chart described. STATEMENT IN WORDS: A statement gives ratio of map Distance to earth Distance, e.g. (i) 1 km = 10 Nm (ii) On this map 1 cm represents 5 km. GRADUATED SCALE: A calibrated scale gives, the ratio of map Distance to carth Distance. NAUTICAL MILES eg- Map/Chart Distance MD/CD
Maps indicate the details of the topography. Pilots can use this for:

Relief. The inequalities in elevation of the surface of the earth represented on the aeronautical charts by contours, hypsometric tints, spot elevations and hill shading, the choice of method being affected by the nature and scale of the chart and its intended use. Contours and Form Lines: Contours are the lines drawn on a map or chart joining places of equal elevation. When these are approximately drawn, they are called form lines. Spot Heights: Is the presentation of spot elevation in feet or meters as indicated below: 1730. Layer Tinting: In order to indicate height intervals, shades of color are chosen which become deeper with increase of height. Thus at a glance, a pilot can know the type of terrain. Hachuring: Hachures are short tapered lines, usually employed to indicate high ground on charts. These lines radiate away from peaks and high ground. In the middle of the tapered lines spot heights showing highest elevation can also be shown. Hill shading: is a method of shading so that if a bright light is shining across the map, shadows are cast by the high ground. Conventional Signs:
o: Civil Land Joint civil and Sheltered
